answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and strictly primary-region scoped, which matches the March case where failover restored latency in minutes with a clean traffic shift. A release 2 hours ago is a plausible cause, but rollback only wins if the build is at fault; failover covers a bad primary-only/canary deploy and a regional infra fault, and historically did not drop writes. Circuit breaking risks failing customer writes at settlement peak; read-replica routing and extra capacity address different (report-load / pre-peak headroom) patterns and are weaker fits. Peak settlement cutover still has downstream reconciliation risk, and release-vs-region remains unproven, so treat those as open.
